title: About
text:
The exchange rate is one of the most important prices in an economy. It acts as an automatic stabiliser and affects all aspects of finance, from trade to foreign flows. Macro traders, central bankers and other finance professionals are therefore interested in the de facto exchange rate decisions of central banks, which can differ from the regime a country announces (Calvo and Reinhart 2002; Ilzetzki, Reinhart, and Rogoff 2022).
Sharma, Sengupta, and Shah (2026) implement the methodology developed in Zeileis, Shah, and Patnaik (2010) for 41 emerging market economies, revealing the de facto behaviour of central banks in FX markets. This website operationalises that work and keeps it up to date.

title: About
About
text:
Objectives

Operationalise the framework of Sharma, Sengupta, and Shah (2026) to build a continuously updating website that shows the exchange rate regimes (ERRs) of emerging markets.
Show the structural break dates of past regimes for an emerging market currency.
Provide a live monitoring system, based on empirical fluctuation processes (efp), that alerts users when there is a potential regime change (Zeileis, Shah, and Patnaik 2010).
Reveal the weights of the basket currencies over time, using exchange rate regressions.
Allow charts and datasets to be downloaded directly from the website.
Implement the framework for all emerging market currencies available in the BIS data (Bank for International Settlements 2026).

title: About
text:
Intended outcomes

A practical website for macro traders, central bankers and other finance professionals whose day-to-day work involves understanding currencies.
Make the framework of Zeileis, Shah, and Patnaik (2010) accessible to a wide audience, from students of finance and economics to FX specialists making business decisions in firms.
Make ERR-related data, such as break dates, \(R^2\), residual standard error and basket weights, easily available to other researchers.
A “living” website that updates on its own, without human intervention, and stays available to anyone interested.
